Planning a Walk-In Shower Remodel in Tampa Bay

By Unique Building Contractors · October 15, 2026

The short answer

A walk-in shower should be planned as a coordinated floor, drain, waterproofing, and enclosure system. An open appearance does not by itself make a shower easy to enter, comfortable to use, or able to contain water.

Define what walk-in means for your household

Some homeowners mean a shower with a low entry; others mean a shower without a door or a flush transition. These are different design goals. Explain the actual need, such as easier entry, room for assistance, or simpler cleaning, before selecting the appearance.

A conversion from a bathtub to a shower requires a review of the existing space and drain arrangement. Do not assume that removing the tub creates enough room for every enclosure or that a flush entry can be installed without changes below the finished floor.

Coordinate water containment before glass

Showerhead position, entry location, floor slope, and enclosure geometry affect where water travels. Discuss how the assembly will manage ordinary use, not just how it looks in a rendering. An open entry can require more room than a compact enclosed shower.

Ask the team to resolve the drain, waterproofing transitions, and any needed floor buildup before finalizing the glass. Glass dimensions are often confirmed after finished surfaces are in place; ask how that measurement and installation sequence affects use of the room.

Make room for maintenance and future needs

Place controls where they can be reached without an awkward movement. Consider a hand shower, planned storage, and appropriate reinforcement where future accessories may be desired. The right choices depend on the user and should be discussed individually.

Review how to clean the enclosure, drain, and corners. For example, an elaborate niche may offer storage but also introduce more joints and surfaces to maintain. Keep product care instructions with the project information and ask what should be inspected during the final walkthrough.

Your planning checklist

  • Describe the entry and access goal.
  • Review drain and floor conditions.
  • Coordinate enclosure measurements.
  • Discuss cleaning and future accessory locations.

Common questions

Can every bathroom have a curbless shower?

That cannot be determined from appearance alone. Floor structure, drainage, available space, and the complete installation details need an individual review.
